key_insight: DiaLLM shows that language models can often recognize dialectal English better than they can generate it, revealing a clear robustness-generation gap. The paper’s main contribution is a controlled framework for studying and improving dialect adaptation across multiple model families and post-training strategies.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the mismatch between dialect understanding and dialect generation in English LLMs. While models may be robust to dialect input, they still tend to output standard, US-leaning English instead of producing dialectally appropriate text.
method: Continual pretraining of three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English.
Comparison of implicit and explicit post-training methods for dialect adaptation.
Evaluation of each post-training approach combined with three different model alignment strategies to enable controlled analysis.
impact: For practitioners, this work clarifies that dialect adaptation requires more than standard robustness measures: generation quality must be evaluated separately. It provides a reusable experimental setup for building and benchmarking models that can produce dialect-aware English more naturally.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing continual pretraining followed by implicit/explicit post-training and alignment strategies.
Side-by-side comparison chart of dialect understanding vs dialect generation performance.
Matrix or grid showing model families crossed with post-training methods and alignment strategies.
Icon set representing dialect input, model training, and dialectal output.
paper_title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
paper_authors: Jordan Painter, Dipankar Srirag, Adarsh Kappiyath, Diptesh Kanojia, Aditya Joshi
